title: Religious Bias Landscape in Language and Text-to-Image Models: Analysis, Detection, and Debiasing Strategies
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures religious bias in language and text-to-image models. Specifically, it assesses underlying stereotypes and negative associations (e.g., with violence, terrorism) disproportionately linked to certain religions. It also examines cross-domain biases where religious bias intersects with demographic factors like gender, age, and nationality.
findings: The study found a pronounced negative bias towards Islam in mask filling and prompt completion tasks across most models, though newer models like Llama 3, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 showed minimal bias. In image generation, there was a tendency to associate Muslims with terrorism and Christianity with violence and other negative attributes. Cross-domain analysis revealed stereotypical links between religions and nationalities (e.g., Islam with Pakistan, Hinduism with India). Negative attributes were also linked to specific age and gender groups within religions. The implemented debiasing techniques, such as positive term augmentation and bias mitigation instructions, proved effective in significantly reducing these biases.
